titles.title: Power in a Blackout
titles.homeQuestion: Could your backup battery keep the fridge running overnight and still charge your phones tomorrow?
titles.headline: How long will your backup power actually last?
description: A 1 kWh battery is sitting in your kitchen. The fridge is running, two phones need charging, and you don't know when the power will come back. What can you leave plugged in overnight?

Learn to measure what your appliances use, check what your power station can run and work out when to recharge. Follow a seven-day plan for an apartment and another for a house with solar and a generator. Then build a power budget for your own home.

example.title: Can a 1 kWh battery run your fridge for three days?

previews.caption: Measure a fridge over 24 hours: record the watt-hours, the room temperature, and whether the AC output stayed on.
A seven-day apartment budget with five days of recharge and two days with none, starting from 750 Wh.

titles.title: When the Tap Runs Dry
titles.homeQuestion: Four people, twelve litres of water and a fountain marked on the map. How do you plan the next 72 hours?
titles.headline: Four people. Twelve litres of water. What do you do first?
description: The tap has stopped. There's a fountain on your map, but you still need to check whether the water is safe, how much you can carry and where to go if your first collection point is closed.

Build a 72-hour water budget, learn how to read a drinking-water advisory and decide when boiling or filtering is appropriate. Follow a household through its first collection trip, then make a plan with your own containers, routes and backup source.

example.title: Four people, twelve litres and one fountain pin

previews.caption: What to do when the notice says boil water, do not drink, or do not use.
The first day's collection plan for a household that starts with 12 litres, and what to do if the pickup fails.
